content.text: Going vegan does not mean giving up satisfying, protein-rich meals. The key is understanding which plant foods are highest in protein and how to combine them to get all essential amino acids.
Supplement with B12, Vitamin D3, and Omega-3 (algae-based) when following a fully vegan diet, as these nutrients are difficult to obtain from plant foods alone.

items.question: How do vegans get enough protein?
items.answer: By eating diverse plant proteins throughout the day: legumes, tofu, tempeh, seitan, edamame, and protein-rich grains like quinoa and amaranth. Aim for 0.8–1g of protein per kg of body weight.

items.question: Is a vegan diet expensive?
items.answer: It does not have to be. Staples like lentils, beans, oats, and frozen vegetables are among the cheapest foods available. The cost increases when buying specialty vegan products, which are not necessary.
